title: The Industrialization of Noise: Why Automated Proof-Solving is the Same Old Dead End
abstract: arXiv:2611.31286v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Nearly fifty years ago, DeMillo, Lipton, and Perlis argued that mathematical proofs are not static, isolated structures of formal logic, but the products of a vibrant, evolving social process of human critique, internalization, and shared intuition. In October 2026, OpenAI challenged this thesis by releasing a massive repository of 722 automated mathematical manuscripts, claiming full or partial solutions to 372 longstanding open problems. This paper examines the immediate crisis through the lens of the original DLP framework. We argue that the sudden, automated overproduction of dense, unreadable proofs represents an industrial pollution of the mathematical ecosystem. By examining the three fatal structural pillars of this automated approach (Specification, Regress, and Utility), we demonstrate that decoupling the act of mechanical solving from the human social process of understanding produces a sterile repository of dead logical art

translated_title: 噪音的工业化：为什么自动化证明求解依旧是那条老死路
translated_abstract: 近五十年前，DeMillo、Lipton 和 Perlis 论证指出，数学证明并非静态、孤立的形式逻辑结构，而是人类批判、内化与共享直觉这一充满活力、不断演进的社会过程的产物。2026年10月，OpenAI 发布了一个包含722篇自动化数学手稿的庞大知识库，宣称对372个长期悬而未决的开放问题给出了完整或部分解答，以此挑战了上述论点。本文通过原始 DLP 框架的视角审视这一迫在眉睫的危机。我们认为，这种密集难读证明的突然、自动化过度生产，构成了对数学生态系统的一种工业污染。通过考察这种自动化方法的三个致命结构性支柱（规约 Specification、回归 Regress 与效用 Utility），我们证明：将机械求解行为与人类理解的社会过程相脱钩，只会产出一个毫无生命力的死寂逻辑艺术仓库。
tldr: 本文借助 DeMillo–Lipton–Perlis 框架批判 OpenAI 发布的722篇自动化数学证明手稿，指出将机械求解与人类理解的社会过程相脱钩，只会造成数学生态系统的“工业污染”，产生死寂而无效的证明仓库。
en_tdlr: This paper invokes the DeMillo–Lipton–Perlis framework to critique OpenAI's release of 722 automated mathematical proof manuscripts, arguing that decoupling mechanical proof-solving from the human social process of understanding amounts to industrial pollution of the mathematical ecosystem.
